title: GLiNER2.5 Doom Journal
heading: Can a zero-shot classifier play Doom without Doom training?
eyebrow: Engineering journal · September 19, 2026 · ViZDoom, GLiNER2.5, ModernBERT, Apple Metal
lede: GLiNER2.5 classifies text against labels it is given at run time, so it can score Doom actions it was never trained on. We gave its Small and Base models the same game observations as the trained ModernBERT policy, first with no Doom examples, then with only their classification head adapted on 32 to 372. 10,500 live decisions later, the answer was yes, partly, and not better than ModernBERT.
description: GLiNER2.5 Small and Base score Doom actions zero-shot and with small trained heads, measured against the trained ModernBERT policy on the same observations.

scope: Where this stands. A small exploratory comparison on one Mac. All five pipelines read the same observations, each in its own text format, and decide through the same legal-action decoder. Training here means adapting only GLiNER's existing classification layers for a fixed 600 steps, not an optimized benchmark. The scripted teacher supplied labels offline; nothing at play time reads it. Every number on this page comes from reports/gliner2-experiment/.
footer: Source, setup and reports: rozgo/doom-sandbox, experiments/gliner2/, reports/gliner2-experiment/ (with a SHA-256 manifest and the raw predictions and game logs). Models: GLiNER2.5 Small and Base from fastino, ModernBERT-base from Answer.AI. Engine: ViZDoom with Freedoom assets. No video was recorded for this experiment.

card.line: GLiNER2.5 attacks and evades with no Doom training, but the trained ModernBERT stays faster and more reliable; a 128-example head helps Small most.
